title: Adaptive schema translation gateway for LLM inference metrics
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers and internal services send a mix of Prometheus scrape metrics, OTLP metrics, and custom inference KPIs with divergent labels and histogram formats. Our current ingestion adapters are brittle: they either reject nonconforming payloads or accept them without canonicalization, causing high-cardinality explosions and inconsistent SLOs.

Proposal: Implement an Adaptive Schema Translation Gateway (ASTG) as a lightweight ingress service that normalizes incoming metric payloads into a canonical inference KPI envelope before forwarding to the metric router. Key capabilities:
- Schema translation DSL: tenant-aware, declarative mapping rules to rename labels, collapse equivalent keys, and move unstructured annotations into controlled strands.
- Histogram normalizer: convert client-specific latency buckets into our canonical latency histogram (and support reservoir sketching for extreme cardinality).
- OTLP<->Prom converter: synthesize Prom metric families from OTLP gauge/counter streams where needed, and tag origin for provenance.
- Circuit and backpressure controls: per-tenant rate limits, malformed-schema circuit breakers, and graceful degradation (drop low-priority labels, switch to aggregated counters) to protect the upstream router.
- Lightweight transform engine: WASM-based filter hooks for tenant-specific redaction, PII removal, and exemplar extraction.
- Contract enforcement mode: allow strict mode (reject) and permissive mode (translate+annotate) to support staged rollouts.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Doing translation at ingress keeps the metric router simple and centralizes schema logic, but adds CPU overhead at the gateway. We'll mitigate with batching, fast-path no-op passthrough for conformant payloads, and a small pool of optimized WASM workers.
- Prefer declarative rules over hardcoded transformations to enable product and SRE teams to update mappings without code deploys. Rule engine will be versioned and validated via unit tests.
- For high-cardinality labels, default behavior is to move unknown label keys to a single JSON blob label (label_fallback) unless tenant opts into expansion, to avoid cardinality blowups.

Acceptance criteria:
1) ASTG accepts Prometheus scrape and OTLP metric streams and outputs canonical KPI envelopes matching the inference-metric contract (label names, histogram buckets, metric name prefixes).
2) End-to-end tests validate correctness on 12 sample client schemas (open-source models, hosted SDKs, dedicated nodes) with zero data loss in permissive mode and clearly logged rejects in strict mode.
3) Under synthetic load (10k rps ingress with mixed payloads) the gateway keeps p95 latency < 120ms and uses <2 vCPU per 1000 rps baseline on the chosen instance size.
4) Circuit breaker engages under malformed flood and upstream router error states; metrics emitted for all degradations.
5) Rollout is feature-flag controlled with canary by tenant and automated rollback on error-rate delta > 0.5%.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 1: Alpha behind internal feature flag. Integrate with test tenants and SRE harness. Validate translation rules for top 6 partner schemas.
- Phase 2: Beta open to a small set of external tenants on permissive mode with metrics-backfill and visibility dashboards.
- Phase 3: GA with contract enforcement opt-in, documenting migration guidance for SDKs and on-prem agents.

Monitoring and dashboards:
- ASTG health dashboard: request rates, p95/p99 latency, CPU/memory, transform error rate, rejected payloads, tenant-level cardinality spikes.
- End-to-end KPI drift dashboard: compare canonicalized metrics vs raw ingestion (sampled) to surface translation regressions.

Docs and artifacts:
- Confluence: designs and mapping DSL reference
- Migration guide for partners and on-prem agents
- GitHub PR for rule engine and WASM runtime

Security and compliance notes:
- WASM transforms run in sandbox with strict syscalls; runtime enforces memory limits per transform.
- Redaction rules enforced at gateway; we will add audit log entries for any PII redaction operations.
